tr: Are you a student? / Yes, I am.
Is this sushi? / Yes, it's sushi.
Do you have tempura? / Yes, we do.
What will you drink? / I'll have tea.
What's this? / That's a book.
Nice weather, isn't it? / It sure is.
Excuse me, where are the stamps? / Over there.
How is your grandmother? / She's doing well.
Where do you live? / I live in Tokyo.
Are you going by taxi? / No, I'm going by train.
Do you have cheese? / Sorry, we don't right now.
Sauce, please. / Here you go.
Would you like some coffee? / Yes, please.
Would you like to come to a party tomorrow? / Sounds good. I'll be there.
Do you like ramen? / Yes, I love it.
Is this your first time in Japan? / No, it's my second time.
Do you have Mondays off? / No, I work.
How much is this? / It's 500 yen.
Nice to meet you. I'm Emily. / Nice to meet you. I'm Tanaka. I look forward to knowing you.
Excuse me, what's your name? / It's Smith.
Long time no see. How have you been? / I've been well.
Here you go. / Thank you.
How many people are in your family? / Four.
Do you have any brothers or sisters? / Yes, I have a younger brother.
Is that a photo of your mother? / Yes, that's my mother.
How much is this rice ball? / It's 150 yen.
Excuse me, what time is it? / It's four thirty.
What time does the meeting start? / At three thirty.
Please, go ahead and eat. / Thank you. Let's eat!
Anything to drink? / Water, please.
Excuse me, what do you recommend? / The tempura. It's really good.
Welcome! How many in your party? / There are two of us.
Excuse me, how much is this? / That's 1,500 yen.
Can I pay by card? / Yes, that's fine.
Do you need a bag? / No, I don't need a bag.
What's that over there? / That's a post office.
What time do you get up every morning? / I get up at six.
What did you do yesterday? / I studied at home.
Did you have breakfast? / No, I didn't eat breakfast.
What are you doing on Saturday? / I'm seeing a movie with a friend.
Tokyo is a big city, isn't it? / Yes, it's very big.
How was the restaurant yesterday? / It was good, but it was expensive.
It's hot today, isn't it? / It sure is.
How was your trip? / It was really good.
Do you like animals? / Yes, I like cats.
Ms. Suzuki, what do you do on weekends? / I usually play tennis.
I'm seeing a movie on Saturday. Would you like to come along? / Sounds good. Let's go.
What kind of movies do you like? / I like scary movies.
Excuse me, where is the station? / Go straight down this street.
Is it far from here? / No, it's five minutes on foot.
Excuse me, does this train go to Shibuya? / No, the next one does.
Do you like traveling? / Yes. I've been to Okinawa.
We're heading out now. / Please wait a moment.
Excuse me. May I come in? / Please do.
What's wrong? / I have a headache.
Excuse me, may I take a picture? / Yes, go ahead.
Are you going to the party tomorrow? / Yeah, I'm going.
Yuki, long time no see! How are you? / Good. And you, Ken?
Want to have lunch together? / Yeah, sure.
Sorry I'm late. / It's fine.
You don't eat meat? / That's right, I don't. Only vegetables.
Would you like some coffee? / No, thank you.
Would you like to go for a drink tomorrow? / Sorry, I can't really...
How is your mother? / She's doing well, thank you.
Please, go ahead and eat. / Wow, that looks delicious!
That was delicious. / I'm so glad.
You're a great cook! / Oh no, it's just something simple.
It's all done. / Just what I'd expect from you!
You're a great singer! / Oh, that's not true.
Thanks for all your hard work. / You too, thanks for your hard work.
That outfit really suits you. / Thank you, that makes me happy.
What a lovely house! / Thank you. Please, come in.
Your Japanese is very good! / Oh no, I still have a long way to go.
You're fluent in Japanese! / You're praising me too much!
That outfit is cute. / Really? Thank you, that makes me happy.
You're beautiful. / Oh, no, not at all.
You're so cool. / Oh, no… thank you.
You have a lovely smile. / Thank you. People tell me that a lot.
That bag shows great taste. / Really? Thanks. (casual reply)
Did you get a haircut? / Yes! You noticed!
You're easy to talk to, Mr. Tanaka. / I was thinking the same about you.
Shall we swap LINE? / Sure.
Want to get dinner sometime? / Sounds good. When suits you?
Are you free this weekend? / I'm free on Saturday.
I had fun today. Can I see you again? / Yes, I'd love to.
Would you like to go see a movie together? / I'd love to go!
I like you. / Me too.
I like you. Will you go out with me? / Yes, I'd be glad to.
You're always so cute. / You're such a smooth talker!
I like you. Will you go out with me? / I'm happy you feel that way. But I'm sorry.
I've always liked you. / Thank you. But I'm sorry, I'd like us to stay friends.
Want to go for a drink sometime, just the two of us? / Sorry, I'm seeing someone.
How about a movie this weekend? / Sorry, I'm a bit busy right now…
Are you Mr. Tanaka? / Yes, I am.
The station is over there. / Ah, thank you.
Was it expensive? / No, it was cheap, actually.
How are you? / Yes, I'm fine.
I'm moving to Japan next year. / Oh, really? That's great!
Look, you can see Mount Fuji. / Wow, it's beautiful!
I made this. / Whoa, amazing!
Oh my, Mr. Tanaka! / Hello.
Are you OK? / Yes. Heave-ho… it's heavy.
Yikes, that's expensive! / It's ten thousand yen.
Thank you for helping. / Oh, not at all.
Do we have everything? / Right, let's go!
This is for you. / Wow, I'm so happy!
Hey, wait! / Sorry, coming! (casual)
Where's Mr. Tanaka? / Hmm, I don't know.
How was the test? / Well, it was OK, I guess.
Your name? / Um, it's Smith.
Um, excuse me. / Yes, what is it?
Press here. / I see, got it.
Apparently tomorrow is a day off. / Seriously? Yay! (casual)
This cake is 100 yen. / Really? That's cheap.
Hello, this is Tanaka. / Oh, hi.
How did the exam go? / Yay! I got everything right!
What's wrong? / Oh no! I forgot my wallet.
Oops, sorry. / No, it's fine.
Are you OK? / Ow, ow… my leg hurts. (casual)
We're done. / Phew, I'm tired.
Your wallet turned up. / Thank goodness! Thank you.
How's the hot spring? / Awesome!
What happened? / Ugh, the worst… the train isn't coming. (casual)
My exam is tomorrow. / Good luck!
I got married. / Congratulations!
